findings.excerpt: The upper endpoint of a c-Cambrian fiber, interval fibers and the explicit formula u_c(w) = pi_{c^{-1}}(ww0)w0
findings.symptom: The CSS-uppercase title banner displays the formula as raw ASCII, including underscore and subscript notation, instead of typesetting it. The item body formula in Statement line 57 is correctly rendered with MathMarkdown.
findings.suggested_repair: Typeset the formula in the title using the renderer-supported math notation or use a plain-language title without a formula.

exact_claims: Lines 43–45: the A2 fundamental alcove has vertices 0, (1,1/√3), (0,2/√3), facet types 1,2,0, and three walls through v1 with six alternating panels of types 2,0.
Line 47: the B2 alcove has vertices 0, e1, (1/2,1/2), facet types 1,2,0 and affine labels m01=2,m02=4,m12=4.
diagram_candidates.kind: Two side-by-side TikZ coordinate triangles for the affine A2 and B2 fundamental alcoves, with typed walls; show the local A2 wall cycle at v1 in an inset.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The example provides exact coordinates, wall equations, corner incidence and panel types for two geometries; a compact coordinate drawing would let a reader check which facet and vertex has each type.
diagram_candidates.specific_content_to_draw_or_check: Plot A2 vertices 0,(1,1/√3),(0,2/√3); mark Hα1,0 type 1, Hα2,0 type 2, Hθ,1 type 0, and at v1 add the three incident lines Hα2,0,Hθ,1,Hα1,1 with six local sectors labeled 2,0,2,0,2,0. Plot B2 vertices 0,e1,(1/2,1/2), label the same three facet types and annotate the matrix labels 2,4,4. Keep A2 and B2 root/scaling conventions separate.
diagram_candidates.assessment: source-supported optional candidate; not a rendering or mathematical defect. The source formulas and coordinate claims were visually checked; no current figure exists.
diagram_candidates.uncertain_vs_confirmed: uncertain optional editorial candidate; no diagram omission is a confirmed defect.

exact_claims: Line 42: among 15 partitions of {1,2,3,4}, exactly {1,3}|{2,4} crosses in cyclic order 1<2<3<4<1; its permutation is the unique missing double transposition.
Lines 44–46: K(w)=w^{-1}c and K²(w)=c^{-1}wc; the item lists K on the 14 interval elements and says K² rotates labels 1→4→3→2→1.
diagram_candidates.kind: Optional square/circle partition schematic for the crossing obstruction, with an adjacent compact Kreweras-complement example.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The text explicitly interprets the type-A interval through noncrossing partitions of four cyclically ordered labels and singles out one crossing partition. The diagram can make that exclusion and the label order immediately visible.
diagram_candidates.specific_content_to_draw_or_check: Place 1,2,3,4 cyclically; draw blocks {1,3} and {2,4} as crossing chords and contrast with a source-listed noncrossing partition such as {1,2}|{3,4}. If showing K, preserve the stated right-to-left convention and verify K((1 2))=(2 3 4) and K² relabels 1→4→3→2→1. Do not imply the crossing partition is in the interval.
diagram_candidates.assessment: source-supported optional candidate; omission is not a defect. The finite permutation maps shown in the text were checked against right-to-left composition; a full 14-element lattice figure is not warranted by this review.
diagram_candidates.uncertain_vs_confirmed: uncertain optional editorial candidate; no diagram omission is a confirmed defect.

exact_claims: Line 38: two m=∞ rank-two blocks have radical R(1,1,0,0) and R(0,0,1,1), corank two, and group D∞×D∞.
Line 40: Q=[0,1]² is bounded by vertical x=0,1 and horizontal y=0,1 reflection walls; its group translates are unit grid squares with pairwise disjoint interiors, and every orbit meets Q once.
Lines 82 and 88: the coordinate reflections are r1(x,y)=(-x,y), r2(x,y)=(2-x,y), s1(x,y)=(x,-y), s2(x,y)=(x,2-y); the generated product map identifies the group with D∞×D∞.
diagram_candidates.kind: TikZ unit-square fundamental-domain and reflection-grid diagram for the explicit D∞×D∞ action.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The source gives the four walls, two commuting infinite-dihedral factors, exact orbit/fundamental-domain claim and tiling conclusion; a coordinate sketch directly supports those geometric assertions.
diagram_candidates.specific_content_to_draw_or_check: Draw Q=[0,1]² with vertical reflections across x=0 and x=1 and horizontal reflections across y=0 and y=1; extend to the integer grid of unit squares and distinguish Q as the unique orbit representative. Check maps from proof step 1.4: r1(x,y)=(-x,y), r2(x,y)=(2-x,y), s1(x,y)=(x,-y), s2(x,y)=(x,2-y). Mark generators from separate coordinate pairs commute and the Coxeter diagram is two disconnected ∞-edges.
diagram_candidates.assessment: source-supported optional candidate; omission is not a rendering or mathematical defect. The maps/orbit claim were checked from the displayed formulas and proof, and no current diagram exists.
diagram_candidates.uncertain_vs_confirmed: uncertain optional editorial candidate; no diagram omission is a confirmed defect.

exact_claims: Line 36 lists the eight elements and all cover relations in [e,c].

Lines 38–42 list the six maximal chains with the six permutations of labels {1,2,3}; line 44 identifies (1,2,3) as the unique increasing first chain; line 46 gives the (1,3,2)→(1,2,3) local replacement.
diagram_candidates.kind: TikZ Hasse diagram of the eight-element rank-three Bruhat interval with cover labels and selected chain highlights.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The example is a finite interval expressly defined by its cover graph and enumerates all maximal chains and label words; a Hasse diagram would make the local rank-two replacement and lexicographic comparison easy to inspect.
diagram_candidates.specific_content_to_draw_or_check: Use levels {1234}; atoms {2134,1324,1243}; rank-two elements {2314,2143,1342}; top 2341. Draw only the nine source-listed rank-two-to-rank-one/top covers plus the three atom-to-bottom covers (12 total), orient upward toward 2341, label edges by deleted positions consistent with source lines 38–41, highlight the increasing chain 2341>1342>1243>1234 with (1,2,3), and distinguish the falling chain with (3,2,1). Check the local diamond on [1234,1342] has middle vertices 1324 and 1243, labels (3,2) and (2,3).
diagram_candidates.assessment: strong source-supported optional candidate; no existing diagram to validate and no omission defect. The finite cover list and chain words were checked from the source; candidate diagram must retain the stated one-line letter-shift convention.
diagram_candidates.uncertain_vs_confirmed: uncertain optional editorial candidate; no diagram omission is a confirmed defect.

exact_claims: Lines 37–39: m(s,t)=6, W=I2(6) has order 12; scaling cs=1, ct=√3 yields Cartan matrix [[2,-1],[-3,2]] and six positive root coefficient pairs (1,0),(0,1),(1,1),(2,1),(3,1),(3,2) with opposite negatives; the alternative scaling gives the transpose and dual orientation.
diagram_candidates.kind: Optional G2 root-system diagram showing the six positive and six negative scaled roots with short/long lengths and both simple-root orientations.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The item explicitly identifies twelve roots, their two squared norms, Cartan matrix and dual scaling orientation. A root diagram can make the long/short pattern and transpose orientation checkable.
diagram_candidates.specific_content_to_draw_or_check: Embed the root plane with inner product prescribed by B, plot ±as, ±at, ±(as+at), ±(2as+at), ±(3as+at), ±(3as+2at); use a_s-length √1 and long-root norm √3 according to line 39, distinguish the two squared-norm classes, and indicate the other scaling as (√3/2)Φ_c^vee with transposed Cartan matrix. Do not plot coefficient pairs as orthonormal Cartesian coordinates.
diagram_candidates.assessment: source-supported optional candidate; no diagram defect. The reflection maps and listed root orbit computations in proof were visually reviewed, but a plotted embedding would need to derive its coordinates from B.
diagram_candidates.uncertain_vs_confirmed: uncertain optional editorial candidate; no diagram omission is a confirmed defect.

exact_claims: Lines 47–49: positive rank-two roots βu1,…,βum are in angular order between extreme rays; initial/final segments are defined by the two endpoint conventions.
Lines 53–57: an inversion set is recognized by requiring each noncommutative rank-two intersection to be empty, an initial segment, or a final segment.
diagram_candidates.kind: Optional rank-two root-sector diagram with ordered rays and shaded initial/final inversion segments.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The central recognition condition is phrased as angular segments in every rank-two root subsystem. A sector schematic makes the endpoint direction and allowed consecutive blocks visible.
diagram_candidates.specific_content_to_draw_or_check: Draw a pointed sector with extreme positive roots and interior roots βu1,…,βum in the stated angular order; show an initial block {βu1,…,βuj} and a final block {βuj,…,βum} as separate allowed subsets, and an interior nonconsecutive subset as excluded. Align reflection order inward from opposite endpoints to the definitions at line 49. Verify the figure is schematic for a finite dihedral subsystem and does not assert all positive roots of W lie in one plane.
diagram_candidates.assessment: source-supported optional candidate; omission is not a defect. The angular endpoint convention and segment criterion were checked in the text; no existing diagram is present.
diagram_candidates.uncertain_vs_confirmed: uncertain optional editorial candidate; no diagram omission is a confirmed defect.

existing_diagram_checks.result: No authored TikZ/tikzcd or embedded image diagrams occur in the 35 assigned item bodies; all capture manifests report tikz_count=0 and diagram_failures=[]. Consequently no existing rendered diagram map, orientation, index, or sign could be checked. Inline coordinate/reflection/root maps, Coxeter labels, cyclic orders, and enumerated tables were visually checked where relevant; no additional questionable sign or index was confirmed.
existing_diagram_checks.math_checks: Checked the A2/B2 alcove coordinates and wall labels, B2 and G2 reflection/root lists and length conventions, the S4 noncrossing/Kreweras convention, rank-three Bruhat cover/chain labels, square chamber reflection maps, and displayed formulas. This is visual/source-supported checking rather than an independent proof audit.

rendering_review.latex_mathmarkdown: Capture metadata records zero KaTeX errors for all assigned items. Visual review found displayed and inline math, indices and signs typeset throughout item bodies except the confirmed raw-ASCII formula in the sortable theorem title.
rendering_review.raw_ascii_math: One confirmed defect: thm-cg-sortable-projection-greatest-element-and-interval-fibers title line 4 prints u_c(w) = pi_{c^{-1}}(ww0)w0 literally. The same expression in Statement line 57 is correctly typeset. No other untypeset raw caret/underscore formula was confirmed.
rendering_review.reference_title_leaks: No unexpected reference-title leak was found. Explicit wikilinks display their reference titles as separate block lines, which is the expected renderer behavior.
rendering_review.technique_banners: CSS uppercase proof-technique banners are expected. No raw-math defect was found in the assigned technique banners.
rendering_review.scratch: No Scratch section or open Scratch content occurs in the assigned ItemBodies. The category capture protocol opens Scratch disclosures before capture.
rendering_review.clipping: No confirmed clipping or lost mathematical content. Tile starts/ends split long content, and the adjacent overlapping tiles were reviewed individually in sequence. No clipping claim was inferred from a multi-image artifact.
rendering_review.wikilinks: Wikilinks intentionally render as block lines; this expected layout is not reported as a defect.

limitations: Read-only local rendering and diagram review. No HTTP/live website, app checkout, external source, build, test, validator, or publication status change was used.
The report checks local frozen screenshots/HTML against source and assignment hashes; it is not an independent re-audit of every proof.
Diagram candidates are source-supported optional editorial suggestions only; none is a confirmed missing-prerequisite or mathematical defect.
